rationale: The round-4 replay ask is PARTIAL at reviewed commit 3a321066. New R3.6 correctly requires non-regressing spec-approve replay semantics, places an absent-only backfill under the R3.3 lock, permits a fail-closed or justified non-regressing alternative, and requires output to distinguish mutation from no-op. AC-16 is red on today's unconditional write for stored implement/review and separately pins the legitimate empty-phase backfill. However, the acceptance surface does not cover all reachable states named by R3.6: it omits stored done even though FindEpicBySpecID deliberately discovers closed epics, and it omits the canonical stored-plan same-value replay whose output must identify a no-op rather than claim a backfill mutation. An implementation can special-case implement/review and empty to pass AC-16 while still regressing done to plan or dishonestly describing a plan-to-plan write. The rest of the document remains grounded and internally coherent in the R6 adversarial/completeness lens, and its open mechanism choices are appropriately chartered to plan stage; this narrow runnable-coverage gap is the remaining blocker. Structural validation reports only the expected no-epic lifecycle-binding warning. bd show mindspec-aytt could not run because the sandbox denied the embedded Dolt LOCK, so no claim relies on that unavailable result.
concrete_changes_required: Extend AC-16 with a stored mindspec_phase=done variant and assert replay leaves done unchanged with honest no-op/refusal output. Also add a stored mindspec_phase=plan same-value replay leg asserting that output identifies no mutation (and does not claim a backfill). Keep the existing implement, review, and empty-phase legs.

findings.title: Round-4 safe-replay ask is specified but not acceptance-pinned across its reachable state boundary
findings.evidence: R3.6 at spec.md:116 names existing epics at implement, review, or done and requires every disposition's output to distinguish mutation from no-op. AC-16 at spec.md:200 supplies fixtures only for implement, review, and EMPTY. The production lookup is not limited to open epics: internal/phase/cache.go:243-247 queries epics with --status=open,in_progress,closed, and internal/phase/derive_test.go:647-667 explicitly proves FindEpicBySpecID returns a closed epic. internal/approve/spec.go:71-76 then takes the existing-epic path and today unconditionally writes plan. Therefore a future implementation that guards only implement/review passes AC-16 while retaining a reachable done-to-plan regression. Likewise, an immediate replay at stored plan is a same-value no-op, but AC-16 does not make dishonest 'phase backfilled' output red for that state.
findings.impact: AC-16 does not fully falsify R3.6 or the prior round's 'implement or later' and mutation-vs-no-op ask. A lifecycle verb could still regress a terminal epic or misstate the most ordinary replay while all written acceptance legs pass.

findings.title: The core non-regressing replay requirement and lock boundary are now explicit
findings.evidence: The 3a321066 diff adds R3.6's absent-only/locked, fail-closed, or justified non-regressing dispositions; requires mutation-vs-no-op output; adds internal/approve/spec.go to Scope for safe replay; and adds AC-16's current-regression and legitimate-empty-backfill fixtures.
findings.impact: The implementation design is no longer free to retain the unconditional later-phase regression; only the two acceptance-boundary variants above remain to make the contract fully executable.

findings.impact: The request for changes is based on the replay acceptance gap, not structural-validation noise.
